guideTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edgers With Wheels (2026)
metaTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edgers With Wheels (2026)
metaDescription: Six cordless lawn edgers that roll on wheels, from dual wheel blade edgers to curb wheel models and wheeled trimmer edgers, compared on tracking and weight.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 8 Inch is the pick for most yards because its curb wheel and brushless motor give the straightest, most repeatable line along a driveway. The WORX WG898.9 is the lightweight pick for small lawns, at about seven pounds without the battery. Skip the wheeled 3 in 1 weed trimmers if you want a crisp wall, since a wheel on a thin blade guides the cut but cannot dig a trench.
introParagraphs: A wheel does two jobs on an edger. It carries part of the tool's weight, so your wrists do less, and it sets the track, so the cut follows the pavement instead of wandering. Those two jobs make the wheel the single most important detail after the blade.

The details vary a lot, though. Some tools have a single curb wheel that rides the pavement, some have a pair of guide wheels, and some are trimmers with a wheel bolted on. This guide sorts them by how well each wheel setup does its job.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 8 Inch Brushless Edger Kit, curb wheel
products.description:
A curb wheel is built to roll on the pavement edge while the blade cuts the turf beside it. That keeps the blade at a fixed distance from the concrete, which gives a straight line without any steering skill, and it also protects the blade from grinding on the curb. The listing says the wheel guarantees the perfect edge every time, which is an overstatement, but the principle holds.

The tool tracks well because the wheel is placed close to the blade and the motor is brushless, so it does not slow and wander in thick turf. Tool free depth adjustment lets you change the cut while standing. Against the goodjob dual wheel design it has a single curb wheel that is better on a straight curb and less steady on a free lawn border.

Check the wheel for packed soil and grit after each use, since a dragging wheel gives a crooked line. Because the curb wheel is the part that touches concrete, it wears too, so look at the tread every season and replace it when it is worn flat, since a smooth wheel slips on damp pavement and lets the blade drift toward the curb. Remove the battery before cleaning. If the tool pulls to one side after a season, check that the wheel is square to the housing and that the axle bolt has not worked loose, since a wheel that is a few degrees off turns a straight curb into a gentle curve over a long drive.
products.bestFor: Straight edges along driveways, walks and curbs.
pros: Curb wheel gives a repeatable straight line
Wheel protects the blade from concrete
cons: Single wheel less steady on a free border

products.name: WORX WG898.9 20V 7 Inch Brushless Edger, dual wheels, tool only

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Cordless wheeled blade edger, bare tool

products.description:
Dual wheels let this edger sit flat and balanced, and the listing says the tool weighs about seven pounds without the battery. Two wheels spread the support, which makes it steadier than a single wheel on uneven ground, and an edge guide plus a blade indicator show where the cut will land.

Because the blade is 7 inches, the cut is narrower and shallower than the Greenworks, so it suits maintenance more than restoration. The tool is sold bare, so you need a WORX 20V pack. Against the goodjob it is lighter and from a known brand, but costs more once you add a battery.

Brush grit from the wheel bearings and check that both wheels spin freely. A sticky wheel pulls the tool off line. On a longer job, alternate the side you walk on so that the tool does not always lean the same way, and swap the battery before it is fully drained, because a tool that is running low can slow and pull to one side.
products.bestFor: Small yards and anyone who wants a light, balanced wheeled edger.
pros: Blade indicator shows the cut line

products.name: goodjob 20V Cordless Lawn Edger, dual guide wheels, 2 batteries
products.description:
Dual guide wheels stabilize the tool in the same way a bicycle's two wheels do, so it resists tipping and tracks well on a free lawn border where there is no curb to follow. A 9 inch steel blade, a 400W motor, three depths and two batteries make it a complete package.

The tradeoff is the 400W motor, which is modest for a 9 inch blade. The wheels help it track, but they do not make it more powerful. Against the WORX it has a bigger blade and two batteries, and against the Greenworks it has two wheels instead of a curb wheel.

Clean the wheels and axles, tighten the wheel bolts each season and check that the blade clears the wheels at the deepest setting. On sloped lawns the two wheel stance helps, but it also means you must keep both wheels on the ground, so work along the slope and not across it when you can, and slow down at the corners where one wheel tends to lift.
products.bestFor: Free lawn borders where two wheels give stable tracking.
pros: Two batteries and a fast charger

products.name: Rawsoil Cordless 3 in 1 Mower, Grass Trimmer and Lawn Edger with Wheels

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Cordless wheeled mower, trimmer and edger

products.description:
This tool folds a small mower, a grass trimmer and a lawn edger into one body, and the integrated wheels are what make the mix work. The listing says the wheels support the tool and give smoother movement along the lawn, so in mower mode it rolls like a light push cutter and in edger mode the wheels set the height and guide the line.

The cost of doing three jobs is that none is done as well as by a dedicated tool. A steel blade edger digs a trench with a vertical wall, while a wheeled multi tool cuts the edge with a thin blade, which is softer. It suits someone with a small yard and a small shed who wants one tool to do everything lightly. Against the iToolMax it adds mowing, but the brand is less established.

Expect the usual routine for a multi function tool: change blades with the battery removed, clean grass from the wheels and head and store it dry. Check that each mode locks in place before you start, since a half seated head vibrates.
products.bestFor: Small yards where one light tool must mow, trim and edge.
pros: Mower, trimmer and edger in one
cons: Softer edge than a dedicated blade edger

products.name: iToolMax Cordless 3 in 1 Weed Wacker with Wheels, 3.5 lbs

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Wheeled cordless trimmer, brush cutter and edger

products.description:
At about 3.5 pounds, this is the lightest wheeled tool by a wide margin, and wheels let you roll it along the ground instead of holding it up. A telescopic pole from 36 to 50 inches suits a range of heights, and two 2000mAh batteries and three blade options are included.

The wheel supports and guides the head, but the blades are thin, so edges are softer than a dedicated edger. It is a good match for light edging, trimming and brush cutting, and a poor one for a deep trench. Against the WORX WG170.9 it uses blades as well as line options and is lighter.

Keep the blades sharp and clean the wheel after each session. Change blades with the battery removed. Because the tool is light, it is easy to let it skip over lumpy ground, so keep both hands on it and let the wheel do its job, which gives a smoother result than lifting the head to place each cut.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want the lightest wheeled tool for general trimming.
cons: Soft edge compared with a blade edger

products.name: Windpost Cordless Weed Wacker with Wheels, 5 in 1, 750W brushless

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Wheeled cordless trimmer with edging mode

products.description:
A 750W brushless motor is a stronger drive than most pole mounted tools, and wheels carry the head along the lawn. The 5 in 1 design covers trimming, brush cutting and edging, and it weighs about 2.5 kg, so it is light, and it comes with two batteries.

The brushless motor gives it better runtime and torque than the brushed trimmers, and the wheels keep the head at a constant height. It still cuts with thin blades or line, so the edge is not a crisp trench. Against the iToolMax it has a stronger motor, but the brand is less established.

Check the wheel bolt and the head for loose parts. Store the batteries partly charged. Since it is a stronger motor on a light frame, keep your hands clear of the head and wear eye protection, as it throws debris with more energy than a weaker trimmer.
products.bestFor: Users who want a stronger wheeled trimmer that can also edge.
pros: Wheels keep the head at height
cons: Soft edge compared with a blade edger

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single curb wheel, as on the Greenworks 40V, follows the pavement edge and gives a repeatable line along a straight curb. Two wheels, as on the goodjob and WORX WG898.9, give stability on a free border. If your edges are mostly along concrete, choose one wheel. If they are along beds, two wheels track better. A mixed yard may justify trying both styles, since the best tool for a driveway is not always the best one for a flower bed, and the difference shows within a few minutes of use.

Small wheels bog in soft turf and chatter on roots. A wider wheel rolls more smoothly and leaves less of a mark. Check wheel diameter and tread, and note whether the wheel rolls freely by hand before you buy. Wide wheels that spread the load leave less of a mark on soft lawns, and a rubber tread grips damp pavement better than hard plastic.

The iToolMax weighs about 3.5 pounds and the Windpost about 2.5 kg, while the WORX WG898.9 is about seven pounds without a battery. A wheel carries some of the weight, but a heavy tool is still fatiguing to turn. Balance the battery weight against the head, and favor a tool whose battery sits close to your hand, because a heavy head with a light handle end makes the tool feel nose heavy over a long border.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Blade edger or trimmer with wheels
buyingCriteria.explanation: A blade edger cuts a trench with a vertical wall, and a wheeled trimmer cuts with thin line or blade. The Greenworks and goodjob are the first kind, while the Rawsoil, iToolMax and Windpost are the second. Wheels do not change what the cutting element can do, so judge the tool first by its blade or line, and treat the wheel as a way to make the cut more consistent.

The WORX WG898.9 lists an edge guide and a blade indicator that show where the cut will fall. A guide helps keep the line straight without constant looking. This is more useful than an extra depth setting for many gardeners, and it matters most when the grass is long and the line of the curb is hidden.

Wheels collect packed soil and grit, which makes them drag and pull the tool off line. A wheel that spins freely is part of a straight edge, and a wobble you can feel in the handle usually traces back to a loose axle or a flat spot on the tread. Check axles and bolts each season and clean after every use.

cards.label: Blade edger
cards.text: A steel blade cuts a trench with a vertical wall. Picks: Greenworks 40V 8 Inch, WORX WG898.9 and goodjob 20V.

cards.label: Wheeled trimmer
cards.text: A line or blade on a pole with a wheel. Lighter and more versatile, but with a softer edge. Picks: Rawsoil 3 in 1, iToolMax and Windpost.

howToChoose.note: Choose a blade edger for a crisp border and a wheeled trimmer for mixed light work.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A curb wheel or edge guide, a stiff blade and a tool that does not pull to one side. Keep the wheel clean and look back along the cut every few meters to catch drift early.

maintenance.why: Soil and grit make wheels drag and pull the tool off line.
Vibration loosens bolts and makes the tool wobble.
A worn blade or thin line cuts poorly and strains the motor, and a tool that strains also drains its battery faster than it should.
It prevents accidental starts, and a pack that has been removed can also cool before you store it.
Moisture rusts axles and blades, so wipe them dry before you hang the tool up and leave it where air can move around it.

faq.q: Do wheels make an edger easier to use?
faq.a: Yes. They carry some of the weight and help the tool track a line, which reduces wrist strain.

faq.q: Is a curb wheel better than two wheels?
faq.a: A curb wheel is better along a straight curb, and two wheels are steadier on a free border.

faq.q: Can a wheeled trimmer replace a blade edger?
faq.a: For light edging, yes. For a crisp trench, a blade edger is better.

faq.q: How do I stop the wheel dragging?
faq.a: Clean it after each use and check the axle for grit. A dry bearing may need a drop of oil.

faq.q: How heavy should a wheeled edger be?
faq.a: Light enough to turn comfortably. The WORX WG898.9 is about seven pounds without a battery, and wheeled trimmers weigh less.

A larger, wider wheel rolls better on soft turf. Small wheels bog in, so if your lawn is soft or lumpy, favor a tool with larger wheels or a wider tread, even if it weighs a little more, because a wheel that sinks pulls the line off course and makes the job slower.
